title: Go2My.Link build programme plan
description: The machine-readable plan for the build programme agreed on 2026-09-21/22 (owner decisions in GitHub issue #243). One entry per piece of work: each is one GitHub issue and one commit. Every item's plan is ALSO posted as an 'Implementation plan' comment on its own issue, so this file is a convenience copy for tooling, never the only record. Validated by tests/unit/build_plan_schema_test.php.

design.description: The binding designs the builders must follow, one per area. Written by the planning agents; a builder reads the part that covers its item.

platform.description: Tiers, the plan-and-pricing admin, the environment-aware switch, the feature registry and how features are gated, and how analytics are stored.

linkspage.description: LinksPage (lnks.page): plan checks, the visitor-facing routine, templates, extras.

fixes.description: The approved fixes and the housekeeping items.

items.description: Every piece of work, keyed by its short key (for example PF-01, LP-07, SX-198, HK-01, CX-01).

key.description: Short unique key. Prefixes: PF platform, LP LinksPage, SX fix, HK housekeeping, SR security reporting, CX review finding.

issue_number.description: The GitHub issue for this item. 0 means an issue still has to be filed; every item in this file has one (see issue_of).

new_issue_title.description: Used only when the issue had not been filed when the plan was written.

new_issue_body.description: As above: the body that was filed.

labels.description: GitHub labels. Only labels that already exist in the repository.

issue_comment.description: Text posted on an existing issue to record the updated scope.

builder_tier.description: The cheapest model that can do this item well. Opus only where the work is genuinely complex. Haiku is no longer used for these items: one Haiku build ignored its instructions and made seven unreviewed commits (2026-09-21).

commit_type.description: The first word of the commit title, which the project's commit style requires.

scope.description: The bracketed scope word in the commit title, for example linkspage, pricing, admin, analytics, security, database.

plan.description: The step-by-step build plan: exact files, numbered migrations and seeds, translation keys, security handling, accessibility, the tests to add, and how to verify. Detailed enough for a Sonnet-tier builder to get it right first time.

acceptance_criteria.description: What must be true before the item is finished. The reviewer checks these.

shared_files_touched.description: Files other items in the programme also edit. Used to keep two builders off the same file at the same time.

depends_on.description: Keys that must be built first.

maxRounds.description: Optional cap on review rounds for this item (documentation items use a lower cap, because review of prose otherwise never converges).

build_order.description: The order to build in: batches of three or four items that do not edit the same files at the same time, foundations first.

batch.description: Batch label and a short name.

keys.description: Item keys in this batch, in build order.

why.description: Why these items are together and in this order.

issue_of.description: Item key to GitHub issue number, filled in when the issues were filed.

amended.description: Items whose plan was rewritten after the owner's second set of decisions (#243, decisions 25-45).

new.description: Items added by those same decisions.

extra_issues.description: Follow-up issues filed but deliberately not built in this programme.

progress.description: What has already been built, reviewed and pushed. Kept current so a fresh session can pick up without reading the whole history.

updated.description: The date this section was last true (YYYY-MM-DD).

branch.description: The working branch every commit goes to.

issue.description: 0 where the commit has no single issue of its own.

commit.description: Short commit ID on the working branch.

next.description: The item keys to build next, in order.

codex_re_review_owed.description: Commits that have had only the stand-in review and still need Codex to look at them.
